payload.rationale: I estimate a 58% chance that November 2026 CPI growth is reported at 0.3% or higher—the single-decimal result required for YES. A reported 0.2% does not qualify; the effective unrounded threshold is approximately 0.25%. Supplied BLS evidence shows August headline growth of 0.4% and core growth of 0.3%, with five of the seven supplied monthly headline readings above 0.2%. This supports a modest lean toward YES, but the small, volatile sample is not a reliable frequency model. August gasoline growth of 3.9% also cautions against extrapolating the headline reading. The supplied FOMC projections suggest persistent inflation and continued economic growth, although annual PCE projections are only indirect evidence for November monthly CPI. My transfer assumption is that underlying inflation remains near its recent pace, while energy and other volatile components leave substantial uncertainty around the threshold. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that gasoline reverses its August increase while underlying inflation cools, bringing headline growth to 0.2% or less. The strongest reason it could be too low is persistent core inflation combined with renewed energy increases, making a qualifying reading more likely than this modest lean implies.
limitations: No September–November CPI readings, current commodity-price forecast, or complete component model are supplied.
The selected seven-month sample is small and volatile; no fitted or calibrated forecasting model is available.
Annual PCE projections differ from monthly CPI in index construction and time horizon.
Supplied source claims are treated as evidence without independent verification; the contract-defined published single-decimal value controls settlement.
